title: A re-encoded Dolby Vision profile 5 film looks right
description: Serves "The picture is as good as the device and the connection allow.". The docs disagree about a re-encoded Dolby Vision profile 5 film: DOMAINS 53 and docs/status.md say it is not mapped (green and purple), docs/transcoding.md says it is tone mapped. Nothing was observed. A wrong picture on every client that does not declare Dolby Vision breaks PRODUCT.md's promise that a re-encoded HDR film looks right on an ordinary screen.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first on a film truly coded for profile 5: an openly licensed profile 5 sample, or a file the task makes itself and shows to be coded so (its picture decoded without the Dolby Vision data comes out wrong, as DOMAINS 53 describes, and right with it). A film that only carries the label does not count. If neither can be had, the task stops and goes to the product owner; it is never closed on a labelled-only file. Frames are taken through a worker's own re-encode on ffmpeg 6.1 and on ffmpeg 9 and compared with the same frames from a reference that applies the Dolby Vision data; recorded in compat/captures with the measured colour difference, no title or path
A re-encoded profile 5 film's colours are within the stated difference of that reference on every supported ffmpeg, without a GPU on the worker; a check fails when the mapping is removed
If no supported ffmpeg can do it without a GPU, the build stops and a brief goes to the product owner with each option priced, keeping the right picture among them
If the observation shows the picture is already right, the task is the check that pins it and the docs
The job's price (Spec.Cost) is at or above its measured CPU
DOMAINS 53, docs/transcoding.md and docs/status.md say the one thing seen; the gap line leaves docs/status.md
